card.name: Stray A glued onto a preceding word
card.fires_on: A lone capital or lowercase letter A (sometimes I) that is stuck directly onto the end of a word or label, as in "Drugs A" before "ffecting" or "Solution A" or "vial a". It marks a broken or run-together label.

modes.label: Drugs split before ffecting
modes.description: The letter A sits right after "Drugs" in interaction headings, with the rest of "Affecting" following.

modes.label: Letter after a product label
modes.description: A single letter follows a solution or vial name, as a version letter or stray character.
modes.example: Anticoagulant Citrate Dextrose Solution USP (ACD) Solution<< A>> is added to tubing sets during apheres

modes.label: Panel letter in a figure
modes.description: A panel letter A appears in a figure caption before B and C.

card.writes: Suppresses name-like endings such as Anderson and Aviv, and promotes separators such as commas and ampersands; the effect is not clearly tied to one meaning.
card.plain: It lights up on a single stray letter A stuck to the end of a word, like the split "Drugs A-ffecting" in interaction headings.
